source.title: From Perturbation Sensitivity to Sparse Autoencoder Feature Interpretation: An EEG Foundation-Model Case Study
source.authors: Yu-Cong Cao; Chen-Qi Li; Ting-Ting Zhu

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether perturbation-responsive SAE latents warrant semantic interpretation and finds that the apparent alpha response largely disappears after controlling for removed signal, while selected latents do not track clean-EEG alpha in the intended direction. This refines and challenges semantic interpretations of SAE latents in the tested EEG setting; it does not test toy-model superposition.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on SAE latent response, stability, and clean-signal correspondence. It does not test feature-capacity competition, overlapping directions, or LLM representations. Quantities used only to define selection or normalization, such as the removed-energy ratios, are not recorded as separate outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses TopK SAEs on frozen EEG backbones as a tool. It tests one inference: whether latents that respond to alpha removal should be labelled alpha detectors. It finds they should not. It never asks whether SAE features are complete, canonical, or the model's own units. It does not compare features across SAE seeds or dictionary sizes. It says it does not rule out structured spatial–spectral features. Its channel-dropout Jaccard measures how robust codes are to input perturbation, not whether features stay the same across training runs. These are related but different constructs, so they go under fits_no_version, not V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that the selected latents are not preferentially important to a linear readout. They state they do not claim no SAE latent is interpretable; the 7.3× alpha signature alone does not support an alpha-representing claim.
record.recipe_differences: This is an EEG SAE validation study using perturbations, distortion controls, and clean-signal correlations; it does not use or reproduce the toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The apparent alpha effect depends on normalization: it remains above one under time-domain distortion normalization but falls below one under removed-spectral-energy normalization. Channel-dropout stability also varies with network depth and backbone.

fits_no_version.finding: Latents selected for responding to alpha band-stop owe that response to signal removed. Spectral-energy-normalized ratio is 0.28, above 1 in 0/27 settings. On clean EEG these latents are slightly anti-correlated with relative alpha (mean r −0.073, negative in 23/27 settings).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Perturbation sensitivity of an SAE latent does not establish what the latent represents; semantic labels need distortion control and observational validation.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE active-set overlap under channel dropout falls from early to late depth in all nine model–dataset combinations. The drop is strongest for DINOv3 (≈−0.35) and mildest for REVE (≈−0.07).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Robustness of SAE codes to input perturbation decreases with depth in EEG and cross-modal backbones.

record.code_released: An anonymized code archive with training and analysis scripts is provided as supplementary material; no URL stated.
record.problems: Most settings use one SAE seed; only the BCI middle setting is retrained under three seeds. The study has no positive control on another physiological axis, tests relative band power as a global frequency property, and notes that band-stop filtering cannot isolate a biological oscillator. Task-readout analyses cover 21/27 settings, and the two distortion normalizations bound rather than eliminate the confound.
record.rows_left_out: The study also reports selectivity–importance correlations and classifier ablations, but these concern task-readout relevance rather than stability or canonicality of representational units, so they are not included for V5.

untested.parts: Toy networks, sparsity-dependent transition, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, geometry.
LLM feature spread across neurons and SAE recovery of LLM features. EEG and vision backbones are not LLMs, and no superposition evidence is reported.
Completeness, cross-seed or cross-size stability, and canonicality of SAE features. Only the semantic labelling of perturbation-selected latents is examined.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 linkage stretches 'canonical units' to cover semantic-label validity. The paper does not test whether SAE features are the model's units. The seed check (three seeds, BCI middle only) concerns how selectivity couples to importance and the order of ablation effects, not whether features match across seeds. The rows_left_out exclusion of the ablation and selectivity–importance results is reasonable.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature sparsity and importance, overlapping directions, and geometry.
Neuron polysemanticity and competition for representational capacity.
Polysemanticity arising through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
LLM feature distribution across neurons and SAE recovery of LLM features.

The study tests stability and the validity of a specific physiological interpretation for selected EEG SAE latents. It does not establish general completeness or canonicality of SAE features across models or properties.
Feature dimensionality and whether features are one-dimensional directions.

rows.subject: 27 settings (CBraMod, REVE, and DINOv3)
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE firing change under alpha band-stop and width-matched sham band-stop, pooled across settings.
rows.note: This is a raw perturbation response; the authors report that it is not distortion-independent, so it does not by itself establish a canonical semantic feature.
rows.check: Alpha/sham perturbation-response ratio tests a semantic labelling inference, not whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units.

rows.subject: 27 settings (CBraMod, REVE, and DINOv3)
rows.operation_detail: Normalized alpha/sham SAE firing-change ratio by time-domain input distortion.
rows.measure: Alpha/sham |∆f| ratio per unit time-domain distortion
rows.baseline: sham band-stop, with each response normalized by its input distortion
rows.note: The normalized response retains an average alpha advantage under this normalization, but not in all settings; the paper says the two normalization choices bracket rather than settle the issue.
rows.check: Time-normalized response ratio. Bears on the validity of the labelling protocol, not V5.

rows.subject: 27 settings (CBraMod, REVE, and DINOv3)
rows.operation_detail: Normalized alpha/sham SAE firing-change ratio by fraction of spectral energy removed.
rows.measure: Alpha/sham |∆f| ratio per unit removed spectral energy
rows.baseline: sham band-stop, with each response normalized by removed spectral energy
rows.note: Under this distortion control, alpha removal does not produce a larger response per unit removed spectral energy than the sham.
rows.check: Spectral-energy-normalized ratio of 0.28 (0/27 settings above 1). This is a distortion-control result on labelling, not V5. The 'absent' state was judged against the wrong target.

rows.subject: 27 settings (CBraMod, REVE, and DINOv3)
rows.operation_detail: Compared active-set overlap under alpha and sham band-stop, including distortion-normalized comparisons.

conditions.value: raw, time-domain distortion, removed spectral energy

rows.note: The overlap ratios show the same pattern as firing change: the raw difference does not persist under the reported normalizations.
rows.check: Code-overlap ratios under alpha versus sham. Same labelling construct, not canonicality or stability of features.

rows.subject: 27 settings (CBraMod, REVE, and DINOv3)
rows.operation_detail: Correlated clean latent activation with trial-wise relative alpha power for alpha-selected specialist-like latents.
rows.measure: Signed Pearson correlation with relative alpha power
rows.note: Latents selected because alpha removal moved them tended to fire on trials with relatively less alpha, opposite to the intended simple alpha-detector interpretation.
rows.check: Signed clean-alpha correlation of perturbation-selected latents (−0.073). Shows the alpha label is wrong, not that SAE features fail to be the model's units. 'Reversed' refers to the alpha-detector hypothesis, not V5.

rows.subject: 27 settings (CBraMod, REVE, and DINOv3)
rows.operation_detail: Compared absolute clean-activation correlation with relative alpha power across specialist-like, fragile, and random-control latent groups.

conditions.value: alpha specialists, size-matched fragile latents, random controls

rows.baseline: size-matched fragile latents and random controls
rows.value: specialists 0.143; fragile 0.246 (greater in 26/27 settings); random controls 0.097
rows.note: The absolute correlation is above random controls but below fragile latents; it does not establish the intended direction of alpha representation.
rows.check: Group comparison of clean |r|. Labelling validation, not V5.

rows.subject: 27 settings (CBraMod, REVE, and DINOv3)
rows.operation_detail: Compared specialist-like latents with activity-matched non-specialists on clean-alpha correlation.
rows.value: specialists 0.143; matched non-specialists 0.101; specialist |r| higher in 27/27 settings
rows.note: Activity matching leaves a small absolute-correlation advantage, but the signed correlation remains negative on average.
rows.check: Activity-matched comparison. Labelling validation, not V5.

rows.subject: 27 settings (CBraMod, REVE, and DINOv3)
rows.operation_detail: Compared relative alpha power on top-activating clean trials for specialist-like latents and matched fragile exemplars.

conditions.value: alpha specialists and matched fragile exemplars

rows.note: The clean-trial difference is small and appears in fewer than half the settings.
rows.check: Top-activating-trial alpha difference. Labelling validation, not V5.

rows.subject: CBraMod, REVE, and DINOv3 across nine model–dataset combinations
rows.stage_stated: frozen backbones; early versus late depth
rows.operation_detail: Compared active-set Jaccard under random channel dropout at late and early depths.
rows.note: Sparse-code overlap was lower at late than early depth across the reported combinations.
rows.check: Input-perturbation robustness of active sets across depth. This is not stability of the learned features across SAE training. Authors call it a secondary architectural observation.

rows.subject: CBraMod, REVE, and DINOv3 across nine model–dataset combinations
rows.stage_stated: frozen backbones; early versus late depth
rows.operation_detail: Compared active-set Jaccard under contiguous channel dropout at late and early depths.
rows.note: Sparse-code overlap was lower at late than early depth across the reported combinations.
rows.check: Same as r9: input-perturbation robustness, not feature stability.

rows.subject: DINOv3
rows.operation_detail: Compared active-set Jaccard under contiguous channel dropout at late and early depths.
rows.note: The text identifies this as the strongest depth-related destabilization among the three backbones.
rows.check: Per-backbone depth robustness (DINOv3). Input-perturbation robustness, not V5. Value is approximate (≈).

rows.subject: CBraMod
rows.operation_detail: Compared active-set Jaccard under contiguous channel dropout at late and early depths.
rows.note: The text identifies an intermediate depth-related destabilization.
rows.check: Per-backbone depth robustness (CBraMod). Input-perturbation robustness, not V5. Value is approximate (≈).

rows.subject: REVE
rows.operation_detail: Compared active-set Jaccard under contiguous channel dropout at late and early depths.
rows.note: The text describes the depth effect as mild for REVE.
rows.check: Per-backbone depth robustness (REVE). Input-perturbation robustness, not V5. Value is approximate (≈).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Alpha-selected EEG SAE latents in the tested backbones, datasets, and depths
reader_labels.reason: The apparent alpha response is not greater than sham per removed spectral energy in any setting, and clean signed correlations are negative on average; this challenges assigning these latents a canonical alpha meaning from perturbation response alone (r3, r5).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SAE code stability under the tested EEG perturbations and depths
reader_labels.reason: Code overlap varies with normalization and depth, so stability and semantic interpretation are conditional rather than established as general properties (r2, r4, r9, r10, r11, r12, r13).
